rows.grounds: first member of compound indicating abundance
second member forming possessive adjective with samṛddhi+
refers to the person described in previous verses
second member of compound object of removal
agent noun describing one who destroys sins
indicates permanence of the sin-removing capacity

items.question: What prosperity and sin-destroying power accrue to the person who attains this liberation?
premises: He also becomes endowed with prosperity.
He becomes a remover of all sins.
This sin-removing capacity is present always.
items.inference: The liberated person gains both material abundance and a perpetual power to destroy all sins.
uncertainties: The possessive form samṛddhimān is represented across two tokens, samṛddhi+ and mān.
items.plain_english: He also becomes prosperous and is always one who removes all sins.
